title: Close the register: the last two open faults
description: F243: _plugin_options is a text scan, so a flag removed properly - parser, tests, and a comment at each site explaining the removal - stays 'carried' and the handbook can advertise it for ever. F232 general: an exemption's REASON is checked against what the other side runs only for the narrow case P19.2 covered.
desiredOutcome: Nothing in the fault register is OPEN: an option is carried when something ACCEPTS it, and every exemption's stated reason is checked against the thing it excuses.

tasks.title: F243: an option is carried when something ACCEPTS it, not when a comment names it
tasks.description: _plugin_options() greps every command doc and every .py for a flag spelling, so removing a flag properly - parser, tests, and a comment at each site saying what went and why - leaves four comments naming it and handbook_drift stays green. That is how docs/handbook.html advertised --include-strangers through a full verify.sh and a full prove-gates sweep. The corpus becomes what ACCEPTS a flag: add_argument string literals read from the AST, plus each command document's argument-hint. A comment is prose about an option, not an option.
files: test__refs.py: a flag named only in a comment is not carried; one argparse defines is

add: test__refs.py: a flag named only in a comment is not carried; one argparse defines is

outcome.summary: _plugin_options grades on what ACCEPTS a flag: AST string constants minus docstrings (a comment is not in the tree at all), the argument-hint of each command document, and --help derived from constructing an ArgumentParser. The add_argument-only rule was tried and measured wrong - materialize-proposal.py reads sys.argv by hand, so --with-deps and --drop-edges are accepted where argparse never sees them, and the narrow rule would have convicted the handbook for naming the product's own options.

verifiedBy: driven live: the handbook re-advertising --include-strangers is now a finding

tasks.title: F232 general: every exemption's reason is checked against the thing it excuses
tasks.description: P19.2 fixed the narrow case - exemption_reason_drift over the gate set. The general shape is still open: an exemption anywhere in the tree carries a reason nobody compares against what it excuses, so a reason can go stale silently. Derive the exemption tables rather than listing them, the way prove-gates derives its lints.
